sentences.text: Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that on 06.10.2020, the appellant took the victim who is a alleged to be a minor aged about 15 years and 1 month, from the lawful custody of her guardian and thereafter committed rape upon her on multiple times.
Learned counsel for the convict/appellant has argued that the appellant has been falsely implicated in this case.
In fact the victim who is a major girl herself had accompanied the appellant and she was not kidnapped by the appellant.
Even the statement made by the victim does not support the prosecution case.
According to the counsel for the appellant, the victim herself went to the house of the appellant and stayed for four days.
Even the victim in her statement before the Court has stated that she made physical relationship with the appellant on her own will.
The prosecution has not been able to prove that the victim was a minor on the date of incident.
It is further submitted that the father of the victim also could not inform the exact date of birth of the victim.
The appellant is in jail since 15.10.2020 and the conclusion of the trial would take some time.
Hence, he prays that the substantive jail sentence awarded to the appellant may be suspended and he may be released on bail.

On the other hand, Mr. Shailendra Sharma, learned Panel Lawyer appearing for the State opposes the prayer for grant of bail and submits that the learned trial Court, after due appreciation of evidence and statement of witnesses have arrived at a finding of guilt of the appellant which warrants no interference.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the bail application.

On 27.02.2024, this Court had directed the State counsel to inform the complainant/father of the victim (PW-2) with regard to pendency of the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

As per learned State counsel, notice has been served to the complainant/father of the victim (PW-2).
Despite service of notice, none has appeared on behalf of the complainant.

Considering the submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, evidence available on record and the fact that even the father (PW-2) of the victim could not depose clearly with regard to the age or the date of birth of the victim, the victim remained with the appellant for four days in the house of the appellant but she never made any complaint to anyone and as such, it appears to be a case of elopement.

Further, the appellant is in jail since 15.10.2020 and the conclusion of the appeal would take some time, as such, we deem it appropriate to allow the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of the appellant.
Accordingly, the substantive jail sentence awarded to appellant- Umashankar Bind by the learned trial Court is hereby suspended.
He shall be released on bail on his executing bail bond to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 25.10.2024.

He shall thereafter appear before the concerned trial Court on a date to be given by the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as may be given to him by the said Court, interval being not less than 6 months, till final disposal of this Umashankar Bind vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72354611/
2 appeal.
Consequently, IA No. 01 of 2024, is allowed.
